name: Antiochus
description: Son of Antiochus Epiphanes, committed to Lysias to be brought up for the kingdom; set up by Lysias to reign in his father's stead and called Eupator; slain by order of Demetrius

points: You don't find out what happened to Menelaus until chapter 13. Menelaus joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made ruler. If I can't be high priest again, I'll be governor.

But the King of kings moved Antiochus's mind against this wicked wretch: one day you are friends, and the Most High says, no, that is not your friend. Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so the king commanded to bring him unto Berea and to put him to death: a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, into which men thrust whosoever was condemned of sacrilege.
